## Summary

Your Mac Mini remotes were down because of a **stale-process bug**, now fixed.

**Root cause:** Someone changed the host-nickname convention in the working tree but didn't restart the long-running supervisor:
- `discovery.py:34` was changed from `*macmini* → "macmini"` to `*macmini* → "mini"`
- `active-dirs.txt` was changed from `dev@macmini`, `FamilyFund@macmini`, … to `dev@mini`, `FamilyFund@mini`, …

But the supervisor process (pid 55373) had been running since **Sat May 23 17:30**, so it was executing the *old* code and still computing its own nickname as `macmini`. When `active-dirs.txt` was edited to `@mini` (~18:14 today), its next tick found no entry matching `macmini`, declared all four servers **"not in allowlist"**, and SIGTERM/KILLed them — `manager.log` shows exactly that wave of `deactivate: ... not in allowlist` lines. It then sat there spawning nothing.

**Fix applied:** `launchctl kickstart -k …com.claudio1.claude-remote-control`. The new supervisor (pid 55630) came up as **`host=mini`**, and all four servers (`mm-dev`, `mm-FamilyFund`, `mm-ai-harness`, `mm-job-search`) are running and **Ready**.

**Two things worth your attention:**

1. **The MacBook (`note`) is probably down for the same reason.** The same rename mapped `*macbook* → "note"` and set `@note` scopes. If note's supervisor is also running pre-change code (deriving `macbook`), its servers got killed as "not in allowlist" too. Run the same `launchctl kickstart -k …com.claudio1.claude-remote-control` on note to confirm/fix. I can't reach it from here.

2. **The convention change is still uncommitted** (`active-dirs.txt`, `discovery.py`, `config.py` show as modified). The running fix is fine because the supervisor imports from the working tree — but you'll want to commit the `@macmini→@mini` / `@macbook→@note` rename so it's permanent and the next person isn't confused by the mismatch.

I saved this as a memory so the `host=<old-nick>` + "not in allowlist" signature is quick to recognize next time.
